question: Fill in the blanks: Established in 1961 within the former Palace of the Maharaja of Patiala, the National Institute of Sports was later renamed as the Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NSNIS) on ______ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**23rd January 1973**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Institute of Sports (NIS) was established in 1961 within the premises of the historic Palace of the Maharaja of Patiala, Punjab.
 
• It was renamed as the **Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NSNIS)** on **23rd January 1973**.
 
• The renaming was done in honor of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, a prominent leader in India’s freedom struggle, whose birth anniversary falls on January 23rd.
 
• NSNIS is widely regarded as the "Mecca" of Indian sports, providing professional training and technical education in various sports disciplines.
 
• It functions under the aegis of the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** and plays a pivotal role in nurturing and developing athletes and sports coaches in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Institute of Sports (NIS) and its importance**:

 
 
• The institute offers advanced training programs for athletes and coaches in a range of disciplines, including athletics, hockey, football, boxing, and wrestling.
 
• It also conducts diploma and certification courses in sports coaching, equipping individuals with the skills to train athletes effectively.
 
• NSNIS has played a key role in producing several Olympians and international-level athletes for India.
 
• It continues to be a hub for sports research and the development of modern training methodologies.
